avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: This year, the City is paying companies to plant and maintain trees on streets and in parks, and it is funding an organization that plants on private and institutional properties. Boroughs are adding their own money, machinery and teams of employees to plant trees. Two boroughs have also allowed construction projects to deviate from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts to plant trees on streets
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees on public land, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The authorized expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, and the trees go to seven boroughs, including Saint-Laurent (423), Verdun (281) and Pierrefonds-Roxboro (265).

etapes.titre: Money to plant on private properties
etapes.texte: The City is paying $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026. The organization and the partners of the Alliance forêt urbaine must plant 14,500 trees and 2,500 shrubs in 2026.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe with operator for $152,916.75 and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams, with a target of about 1,000 trees planted in 2026.

etapes.titre: Two exceptions to the tree rules
etapes.texte: Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve allows a company to expand its building at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening, instead of the required 40 trees and 25%, with the company compensating on its other properties. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

etapes.titre: Work at parc Pratt, in Outremont
etapes.texte: Outremont awards URBEX CONSTRUCTION INC. the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, water retention and new pathways. The authorized expense is $800,416.17, taxes included, funded mainly by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit progress reports on July 31 and October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve's tree plantings take place from April or May to November 2026.
Watering, maintenance and replacement of trees planted under the central city contract continue until the end of November 2029.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to clean streets, lanes, sidewalks and bike paths in spring. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes a spending of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four vacuum sweepers and three tanker trucks [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is entrusting companies with the upkeep, cleanliness and snow removal of square Viger, place des Montréalaises and six squares including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending the snow removal contract for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

etapes.titre: Staff for Verdun's snow disposal site
etapes.texte: Verdun is offering city council to provide the staff for the snow disposal site itself during snow loading operations, for 2025, 2026 and 2027. The positions concerned are gatehouse attendants, sewer chute monitors, and drivers and operators.

Montréal-Nord approves an additional spending of $106,150.97, taxes included, for the rental of a grader with operator [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard is drawing $200,000 from its surpluses to pay for staff and abrasives [CA26 13 0121].

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Léonard indicates that the adoption of its snow removal by-law is planned for September 8, 2026, with a notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The extended towing contracts start on November 15, 2026.
The rental of equipment with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie resumes on November 1, 2026 and runs until March 31, 2027.
The extension of the grader rental contract in Anjou covers November 15, 2026 to April 15, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.

etapes.texte: The City is raising the loan for the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000. The money is to be used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen plant.

The City is awarding contracts to FER-PAL Construction and Services d'infrastructures Vortex to rehabilitate secondary water pipes using trenchless methods and redo the pavement, on streets in more than a dozen boroughs. These projects include replacing lead water service connections on both the public and private sides.

The City is awarding Pronex Excavation the reconstruction of a 500 mm water pipe on rue Guy, and Les Entreprises Michaudville work on rue De Champlain, where a 1,200 mm pipe installed in 1927 is being replaced. It is adding $12,144,522.14 in contingencies to Pomerleau's contract for the rue de la Cathédrale pipe, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019.

aSurveiller.texte: Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant expected in 2029; contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 must be completed by the fourth quarter of 2028.
End of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe postponed from December 2026 to March 2027.
Leak detection on main pipes: work from July 2026 to June 2028.
Rehabilitation of the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord: work starting in September 2026, to be completed no later than December 18, 2026.
Rue Guy project expected from the second quarter of 2026 to December 2027.
Federal grant of up to $128.3M conditional on completing infrastructure by 2031 in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump site, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, and electrical upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical facilities linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also asking Québec for financial help for an east-west pedestrian and bike link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redeveloping rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for financial help of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge of about 150 metres (CG26 0121). The project also includes stormwater management structures and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The agglomeration approves the construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also hires two companies to handle general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers and waterworks, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, for $296,349.21 more, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the development of parc Frédéric-Back (CG26 0320).

The borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes a total expenditure of $574,845.80. The project involves two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, soils, interior partitions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: infrastructure delivery in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses expected to be put into service in winter 2027.
The call for projects under the Ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: work in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to rebuild heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The application does not commit any spending; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, upgrading its light fixtures to standards, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural areas
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération (registry of natural areas protected and contributing to biodiversity in the agglomeration), with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 summary of areas.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, road resurfacing, and replacement of the guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected end of work on the stone walls on chemin de Senneville: July 10, 2026.
Submission of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
DarkSky International's response on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: This year, the City is lending municipal buildings free of charge to organizations so they can open warming centres, and is funding organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also renewing a Ville-Marie public works team that carries out cleanliness interventions related to homelessness in other boroughs. In June, it set up a framework for accepting private donations for housing and shelter projects.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter of 2025-2026: the former church at 5600, 12e Avenue in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the former Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. All three loans end on April 30, 2026.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in place from January 5 to February 6, 2026, in municipal facilities and their surroundings. Ahuntsic-Cartierville confirms the continuation of COHAB inc.'s contract to operate a warming centre during the winter of 2025-2026.

etapes.titre: Funding for organizations over three years
etapes.texte: The City grants $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and adds $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028. The projects focus on the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, coexistence in public space, and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Public works team offered to boroughs
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie offers other boroughs the services of a public works team dedicated to cleanliness related to homelessness, for 12 months starting in spring 2026, with a budget of $931,328 for 2026 coming from the Service de la diversité et de l'inclusion sociale. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve and Le Sud-Ouest accept the offer.

Lachine, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Ahuntsic-Cartierville in turn accept the Ville-Marie team; the agreement with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs from May 15, 2026 to May 15, 2027. City council adopts a declaration in support of people experiencing homelessness and in recognition of the organization Maison Mobile.

The City adopts a mechanism to govern private cash donations intended for housing, shelter and social coexistence projects for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Donors do not choose which project is funded, and the City may refuse a donation.

aSurveiller.texte: The agreement on the public works team with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs covers a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: The City is approving the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, transferring or purchasing land for social housing, and paying grants to organizations that build affordable housing. It is also amending the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units. The urban agglomeration council approves that of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households.

etapes.titre: Two parcels of land for social housing
etapes.texte: The City obtains from the Government of Canada, at no cost, half of the rights to a 3,658.8 square metre parcel of land on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a parcel of land at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, where 26 housing units are to be built.

The City signs two funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary housing and help finding housing. It adds $877,312 to its assistance to Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit seniors' building and grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project.

After a public consultation meeting held on February 26, 2026, city council amends the by-law on social, affordable and family housing: it will now only apply to projects larger than 18,000 square metres and will require 20% non-market housing. Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its by-law on fees for temporary occupation of public property related to social and affordable housing projects.

etapes.titre: Purchase of land in Le Sud-Ouest
etapes.texte: The City purchases, for $9,293,113, a vacant 1,535.1 square metre parcel of land east of rue Chatham and north of rue William, for social housing purposes. It also removes eleven lots in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest from the list of properties subject to the right of first refusal for social housing.

etapes.titre: 350 housing units at Angus, 72 housing units in Rosemont
etapes.texte: The City grants $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel to build 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build a 72-unit building on the "Solotech" site, on 2e Avenue.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline for the sale of the land at rue Chatham and rue William: August 12, 2026.
SHDM project on 2e Avenue: public call for tenders in late summer or early fall 2026, construction to start by the end of 2026, delivery in May 2028.
Affordable housing at Technopôle Angus: occupancy expected by April 30, 2027 at the latest.
Construction sites announced by the SHDM: De Maisonneuve in Ville-Marie in spring 2026, Jardin des Prairies in fall 2026, and a 72-unit project at the corner of Gilford and 2e Avenue in fall 2026.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council approved the modification of two leases for land south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. One serves as parking for Société de transport de Montréal employee vehicles, the other as paid parking for members of the clicknpark app.

The City is extending the free loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to Ville en vert for its vegetable garden, a real estate subsidy valued at $121,100 (CM26 0447). City council also agreed to prepare the lease itself with Îlot 84 for a 78,244-square-foot lot at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, free of charge.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82 taxes included. The work affects sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the Louvain eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name came from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024 by the borough and the local heritage and toponymy committee.

etapes.titre: New street, utility networks and decontaminated soil
etapes.texte: The contract goes to Charex inc. to build an eco-district road with sewer, water main, roadwork, lighting and environmental soil management, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336 taxes included. The City is adding $2,007,312.15 net, from the environmental liability reserve, to remediate the soil of the former gas station on the Louvain Est lot. A one-year free lease is also granted to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine for sunflowers and a greenhouse.

aSurveiller.texte: The temporary Esplanade - Louvain space, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, is supported for the period from June 9 to December 31, 2026.
The Société de transport de Montréal parking lease begins on October 1, 2026, for three years, for at most 92 days per year.
The land loan to the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2027.
Ville en vert's vegetable garden can remain in place until December 31, 2027.
The rue de Louvain construction site between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel takes place in three phases, from May 2026 to August 2028.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named by the time developments are completed, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: The City changed collection schedules and frequencies in several boroughs, and extended contracts for treating food waste, collection by containers, and container transport for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It also purchased collection bins, awarded companies contracts for hydro-excavation work with waste treatment, and received the 2025 waste management reports.

etapes.titre: Extensions of collection and treatment contracts
etapes.texte: The City extended two contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. by six months to treat food waste, with an additional expense of $3,269,055.43 taxes included [CG26 0045]. It also extended by 12 months the contracts for garbage collection in front-loading and semi-underground containers, and the contract for the supply and transport of containers for the écocentre Saint-Laurent.

The executive committee changed the days, schedules and collection sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30, and every week from May 1 to October 31 [CE26 0466].

etapes.titre: Purchase of bins and support for residents
etapes.texte: The City entered into agreements with USD Global inc., Orbis Canada ltée and Plasti-Bac inc. to supply and distribute collection bins for residents. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Ville en vert to inform and raise awareness among residents of buildings with eight units or fewer in the districts of Ahuntsic and Sault-au-Récollet, where the frequency of garbage collection is being changed, for $230,108.67 taxes included [CA26 09 0141].

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal authorized the removal of two dwelling units in the basement of 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest to set up a waste storage room of at least 28 m² and 32 bicycle spaces. Le Sud-Ouest lifted the requirement to set up a drop-off area on the site of the future building at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest, and the executive committee approved an agreement with Tricentris, which is paying $43,773.61 for a program to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations.

The urban agglomeration council took note of the 2025 waste management report and the accountability report for the 2020-2025 Master Plan: 415 kg of waste per person, 48% of materials diverted from disposal, and 29 of the 49 actions completed [CG26 0311]. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Saint-Laurent and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce filed their expense reports for the activities delegated to them.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until September 30, 2026.
The container collection contracts and the écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract are maintained until October 31, 2027.
The program to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The hydro-excavation contracts end on December 31, 2028.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new district on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water supply system for the Namur–De la Savane sector.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not entail any financial compensation and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer remain the same.

The City acts as guarantor for a $2,000,000 loan from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, a not-for-profit organization, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and management of the district's public assets.

City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan by-law for soil remediation, sewers and water supply, street redevelopment, professional fees and land purchases. This work is meant to serve the first phase 1 lots, intended for social, community and affordable housing.

etapes.titre: $12,000,000 loan for the water supply system
etapes.texte: A second loan by-law, for $12,000,000, funds the construction of water supply trunk mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It covers plans and specifications, soil studies, surveying, decontamination, land purchases and a first batch of work.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline set by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site.
2031: the $128.3M federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by this date.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is having parks redone in various places across its territory: play areas, water play areas, trails, sports fields and dog parks. It is awarding design and work contracts, adjusting contracts already underway, and paying for the decontamination of land where parks will be built. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is repairing structures, submitting an application for an international designation, and adding an area to the registry of protected natural environments.

etapes.texte: The City is entrusting the winning team of an architecture competition with the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of the parc Le Prévost, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil studies before redoing the play areas of the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

etapes.titre: Work and protection in the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and is awarding a contract to rebuild a culvert under this same road, in the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and is adding the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the registry of protected natural environments.

Boroughs are awarding contracts to redo parks: parc à chien Lucie-Bruneau in Anjou, parc Mackenzie-King in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, parc canin Alexis-Nihon in Saint-Laurent, parc Monseigneur-Langlois in Verdun and parc Percy-Walters in Ville-Marie. Outremont is paying $150,000 to redo the play module at the parc-école Saint-Germain.

City council is transferring a section of the former rue Eadie, measuring 810.2 m², to the parc Campbell Ouest, in the Sud-Ouest. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a work contract for the parc Denise-Morelle and is paying an additional amount to the project's architects, while LaSalle is entrusting the redevelopment of the parc J.O.R.-Leduc.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026, installation of the artwork in 2028.
Urban Night Sky Place application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site brought into compliance in April 2032.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work expected in June 2027.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a continuation in spring 2027.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amended its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revised three by-laws, and Saint-Léonard two, following public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough changed the heights, uses and lot coverage ratio in the area bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increased the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa, to follow the Plan's density rules.

Following the public consultation on March 25, 2026, the borough adopted a by-law covering urban planning, special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. The text allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and permits public transit stations in category E.1 areas.

etapes.titre: Requests for delay to the ministère
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requested twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requested six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

aSurveiller.texte: Mid-June 2026: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials, then hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.
June 16, 2027: deadline set by the ministère for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; Ahuntsic-Cartierville has requested the same deadline.
June 17, 2027: deadline given to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood police stations, city council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: The City funds and equips the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: a loan for specialized equipment, the purchase of motorcycles and ammunition, service contracts for its buildings and its IT system. It is also renewing leases for neighbourhood police stations and SPVM premises, and lending police officers to the Gendarmerie royale du Canada and the Sûreté du Québec. Some borough councils receive reports from neighbourhood police station 7 and adopt motions of support for the SPVM.

etapes.texte: The City is buying patrol motorcycles for a total expense of $550,899.04, taxes included, and is entering into an agreement for the supply of 9 mm practice ammunition used for firearms training. It is also accepting an $8,000 grant from the Department of Justice of Canada for an information campaign on sexual assault during the Victims and Survivors of Crime Week, from May 11 to 15, 2026.

The City is extending janitorial services at the headquarters, mail courier services and maintenance of the computer-aided dispatch system software. It is also awarding a contract for meals for detained persons and agreements for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The "Fèves au lard" fundraising day for neighbourhood police station 46 takes place on October 23, 2026.
The extension of the dispatch system software maintenance contract runs until May 4, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating system in the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.
The contract for meals for detained persons runs until April 30, 2029, with a 12-month extension option.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docking points and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed at street worksites. It is also funding the repair of existing bike lanes, including the REV Lajeunesse, and regularizing rents for Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their own bike lanes.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes a $100,000 expense, including taxes, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended in particular for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, including taxes.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, including taxes, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical works and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, including taxes.

City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, including taxes, with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 pieces of land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, for a total rent of $46,896, including taxes, to lease about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for use as a bike path.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of the repair of sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike path works under the 2019 Bike Plan. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contract awards in June and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; sections along the route are targeted by roadway works in Ville-Marie.
The repair of the bike lane on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is listed at $570,000 in 2027.
The sustainable mobility corridors worksite resumes in spring 2026, for delivery in spring or summer 2026.
